common.startersNote: Replace the text in [square brackets] with your own.
common.title: Title
common.subtitle: Subtitle
common.author: Your name or organisation
common.outlineIntro: Write your slides as text. A line that starts with # begins a new slide. Lines that start with a dash become bullet points.
outlineHelp: # Title: a new slide with bullet points
- Text: a bullet point (a plain line works too)
== Heading: starts a column. Use two for a two-column slide
| a | b |: a row of a table. The first row is the heading
quizHelp: Q: question: a new quiz question
A) option: its options, one on each line
Answer: B: the answer, shown after the question or at the end
common.agendaHint: A list of your sections after the title slide.
common.tooMany: Only the first {max} slides are kept.
common.previewNote: This is how the slides will look. PowerPoint may break lines a little differently. Replace the prompts in [square brackets] before you present.
common.bracket: Some text is still in [square brackets]. Replace it before you present.
common.failed: The file could not be made. Please try again.
common.notSaved: Nothing you type here is saved or uploaded. Start again goes back to the original starter.
fileNotes: The file is a normal .pptx that opens in PowerPoint, Google Slides, WPS Office and LibreOffice Impress.
Titles are real slide titles, so the outline view and screen readers can find them.
It has no macros, no pictures and no links to the internet.
common.startedAgain: All boxes and the outline are back to the starter text.
common.designHint: Pick a design. The preview below changes straight away. You can still change the font.

gk.label: General knowledge
gk.hint: Questions with four options and the answer after each.
gk.title: Quiz time
gk.subtitle: [Team or class]
gk.outline:
Q: Which is the largest planet in the Solar System?
A) Earth
B) Jupiter
C) Mars
D) Venus
Answer: B) Jupiter
Q: How many days are there in a leap year?
A) 364
B) 365
C) 366
D) 367
Answer: C) 366
Q: Which gas do plants take in from the air?
A) Oxygen
B) Nitrogen
C) Carbon dioxide
D) Hydrogen
Answer: C) Carbon dioxide
Q: How many sides does a hexagon have?
A) 5
B) 6
C) 7
D) 8
Answer: B) 6
